sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: MASC/ASCF AGI asymmetry applied to one stated partnership, asked as a total (the aq-02486 Medium recipe); target medium; rev 0 quick test "too easy" (user report, Feedback log); rev 1 is the one focused repair for that mechanism; platform pending.
- Dependency plan: D02 (MASC): $900,000 average-AGI bar for 2021-2023 with the 75 percent farm-income exception (L274-275); farm income items (1)-(13) (L118-131) and the conditional inclusion of production inputs and services once items 1-12 reach 66.66 percent of AGI (L102-105), production inputs defined to include seeds (L144); $125,000 cap excluding joint ventures and general partnerships (L276); attribution of a legal entity's payment to members (L277); legal-entity definition including general partnership (L133). D07 (ASCF): the same bar with no exception (L148, L365), $250,000 cap per person, legal entity or JV/GP member (L147, L363), partnerships of citizens or resident aliens eligible (L309). Operations: farm share 70 percent crops (item 1) >= 66.66 percent, so seed sales count: farm income 100 percent >= 75 percent; 4 x 125,000 = 500,000; 3 x 250,000 = 750,000; 500,000 + 750,000 = 1,250,000.
- Universe: two programs, four partners; only the over-$900,000 partner differs, and only in ASCF.
- Necessity: D02 alone gives the MASC half (searched "MASC", "125,000", "75 percent", "66.66", "production inputs", "farm income", "attributed", "general partnership" across D01-D07: payment-limit, AGI and farm-income text exists only in D02 and D07; D02's "$250,000" is a fn 17 sales boundary). D07 alone gives the ASCF half (searched "ASCF", "250,000", "900,000", "member of a joint venture": D07 only); D07 is a June 1, 2026 rule. Each document contributes a nonzero half, so dropping either changes the total.
- Selected-lever checks: route table recomputed by script (2026-10-09) over cap mode (per member, partnership once, none) x seed sales (counted, excluded) x exception (not carried, carried) in each program: totals 0; 125,000; 250,000; 375,000; 500,000; 625,000; 750,000; 875,000; 1,000,000; 1,125,000 (three routes, incl. seed excluded); 1,250,000 (one route: per-member caps, seed counted, exception not carried); 1,500,000. Four partners keep every two-error route off the gold.
- Targeted failure modes: Look-alike measure: crop income alone (70 percent) taken as farm income misses D02's 75 percent exception; the partner then loses MASC too: 375,000 + 750,000 = $1,125,000. Wrong jurisdiction or scope: carrying D02's exception into D07's bar gives 500,000 + 1,000,000 = $1,500,000. Not declared: capping the partnership once ($375,000), set by the question but solved by the easier solver on rev 0 (quick test), kept in this table only; partnership disqualified from ASCF ($500,000), unobserved.
- Calculation verification: script sums and the route table above; whole dollars, no rounding, no dates.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no document names the other program; the bundle overview mentions the $125,000 and $250,000 limits separately and no combined or partnership figure; no passage prints 750,000 or 1,250,000. "seed" occurs a dozen times in D02 (background input costs, vegetable/grass seed crops, excluded oilseeds, documentation records); only L144 ties seeds to production inputs, which only L102-105 bring into farm income. Shortest valid route: the two AGI rules, the farm-income definitions with the 66.66 percent clause, the two caps with their partnership wording, then three sums.
- Precision/readings: "most" settles unstated facts (other partners' AGI and citizenship, shares, sales, acres): with per-member caps the supremum is independent of ownership shares, and ASCF's citizen/resident-alien partnership condition (L309) is met in the best case. "Selling seed to farmers" counts under either reading: seed the partner grew is item (1) crop income (MASC lists vegetable and grass seed as specialty crops), and resold seed is a production input admitted by the 66.66 percent clause; the clause's "may also take into consideration" and item (13)'s discretion can only add farm income, so the gold does not rest on discretion going one way. Crops at 70 percent clear the 66.66 percent gate with room. The AGI years are not in the question because both programs fix the same 2021-2023 average (D02 L274, D07 L148). "General" is kept: limited partnerships are legal entities the caps do not exclude. MASC proration or a lowered limit can only reduce payments. D07 administers AGI under 7 CFR part 1400 subpart F; the bundle prints no exception there. ASCF's actively engaged and foreign-person provisions do not apply (D07 L149); D02 imposes no actively engaged test.
- Completeness: complete capture, no gaps (notes/intake.json); all seven texts read by the caller.
- Style/set review: 33 words, one ask, above the 20-29-word cluster of recent questions (length-spread concern); "70" is printed in D02 at character 8,020 and "66.66" at 12,843, both form-readable. Siblings i02/i03 share this family; submit at most one.
- Warnings answered: Step 2's "75" is printed in Doc 2 only at character 43,079, inside the quoted evidence: an expected form false alarm.
- Revision history: rev 1 (2026-10-09) answers rev 0's quick test ("too easy"): rev 0 said "all from farming", which settled MASC's exception inside the question; rev 1 gives the partner's income as 70 percent crops and the rest seed sold to farmers, so D02's definitions section (the 66.66 percent clause and the production-inputs definition, far from the AGI rule) decides it. Gold, documents, tags and caps unchanged; Steps 3-4 added, failure mode 1 now the farm-income measure. One focused repair for this family: a second too-easy result retires it.

sections.question: What is the most MASC and ASCF combined could pay a four-partner general partnership if one partner's average AGI exceeded $900,000, 70 percent from crops and the rest from selling seed to farmers?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 7, payment limitation and payment eligibility section): for ASCF, a person or legal entity other than a joint venture or general partnership "is ineligible for ASCF Program payments, directly or indirectly," if average adjusted gross income for the 2021, 2022, and 2023 tax years exceeds $900,000. Doc 7 states no farm-income exception to this bar.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 2, Average AGI Limitation and Payment Limitation): MASC applies the same average AGI bar to the same tax years, "unless the person or legal entity's average adjusted gross farm income is at least 75 percent of their average AGI."

Step 3. Source input (Doc 2, Definitions): income derived from farming includes "(1) Production of crops"; if the average adjusted gross farm income "derived from items 1 through 12" is at least 66.66 percent of average AGI, the average adjusted gross farm income "may also take into consideration" income from "The provision of production inputs and production services to farmers", and "Production inputs mean material to conduct farming operations, such as seeds".

Step 4. Application (Doc 2): the partner's crop income is item (1) income and makes up 70 percent of average AGI, at least the 66.66 percent of Step 3, so the seed sold to farmers (production inputs) also counts as farm income. All of the partner's average AGI is then farm income, the partner meets the Step 2 exception and stays eligible for MASC.

Step 5. Application (Doc 7): the same partner's average AGI exceeds $900,000 and Step 1 allows no exception, so no ASCF payment can reach that partner directly or indirectly. At most, the other three partners remain eligible: ASCF accepts a partnership "consisting solely of citizens of the United States or resident aliens", and the question states nothing else against them.

Step 6. Source input (Doc 2, payment limitation and attribution): the $125,000 MASC cap binds "a person or legal entity, other than a joint venture or general partnership", and "A payment made to a legal entity will be attributed to those members who have a direct or indirect ownership interest in the legal entity"; the legal-entity definition lists general partnerships. Each of the four partners is therefore capped separately.

Step 7. Calculation (Doc 2): MASC maximum in dollars with all four partners eligible (Steps 4 and 6): 125,000 + 125,000 + 125,000 + 125,000 = 500,000.

Step 8. Source input (Doc 7, payment limitation rule): "A person, legal entity, or member of a joint venture or general partnership" cannot receive, directly or indirectly, more than $250,000 under the ASCF Program, so each eligible partner is capped separately.

Step 9. Calculation (Doc 7): ASCF maximum in dollars for the three eligible partners (Steps 5 and 8): 250,000 + 250,000 + 250,000 = 750,000.

Step 10. Final answer (Doc 2 and Doc 7): most the partnership could receive from MASC and ASCF combined, in dollars (Steps 7 and 9): 500,000 + 750,000 = 1,250,000.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Look-alike measure
How a careless solver fails: Takes the wrong line item

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Wrong jurisdiction or scope
How a careless solver fails: Misapplies a rule or premise

Why these are traps: Measure: Doc 2 counts seed sold to farmers as farm income once crop income reaches 66.66 percent; crops alone (70 percent) miss the 75 percent exception, giving $1,125,000. Scope: Doc 7's $900,000 bar has no exception; carrying Doc 2's into ASCF gives $1,500,000. Gold: $1,250,000.
